summary: A class defines a new type with its own fields. new creates an object from the class and runs its constructor.
notes: constructor() runs every time you call new Student().
this.name = "" creates the name field on the new object. Writing name = "" without this. causes ReferenceError: name is not defined.
maya.name = "Maya" changes only maya. jordan keeps its own empty name. 0.0 prints as 0.
pitfall: Writing const maya = Student(); without new causes TypeError: Class constructor Student cannot be invoked without 'new'.
contrast: JavaScript creates fields inside constructor() with this.name, the way Python uses self.name inside __init__, and does not declare them at the top as Java does. Like Java, you create the object with new.
